angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 605,259 km at 116.78 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.5632 +/- 0.0189 mas (same row, RUWE 1.19): 116.78 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.87 +/- 0.04 solar radii from Hellier et al. 2017, the stellar radius of WASP-140 b's parameter set from Hellier et al. 2017 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017MNRAS.465.3693H/abstract): 605,259 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Hellier et al. 2017, the stellar mass of WASP-140 b's parameter set from Hellier et al. 2017 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017MNRAS.465.3693H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5300 +/- 100 K from Alexoudi 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-140 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AN....34324012A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Alexoudi 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-140 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AN....34324012A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-140.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.513, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
